# UAE Corporate Tax: 2026 rates, scope, Small Business Relief, free zones and filing

Tax year 2026. In the UAE the tax period is the business's financial year, so "2026" here means tax periods running in 2026 (for most businesses, the calendar year 1 January to 31 December 2026). The operative rules below were read on 1 November 2026 in the source scopes listed at the end; held methods are not confirmed. A short dated section covers returns for periods ending in 2025.
## Scope and who this is for
This skill covers federal Corporate Tax under Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 for:

- UAE companies and other juridical persons, including free zone companies, and foreign companies effectively managed and controlled in the UAE. Subject to Article 4 exemptions, they are within the Corporate Tax regime without a turnover threshold; the rate bands still apply. There is no natural-person turnover threshold for a juridical person (Corporate Tax Law, Article 11(3)).

- Individuals (natural persons) running a business in the UAE: sole establishments, freelancers and other self-employed people. They are taxable only when their total business turnover is more than AED 1,000,000 in a calendar year (Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023, Article 2).
- Small businesses deciding whether to elect Small Business Relief.
- A summary of the domestic minimum top-up tax for large multinational groups. The detailed work is referred out.

Wages are outside federal Corporate Tax for a natural person. Wages, personal investment income and real estate investment income are not business income for an individual, whatever the amount, and do not count towards the AED 1,000,000 test (Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023, Article 2(2)).
The skill does not cover VAT, excise tax, Emirate-level taxes, tax groups, business restructuring relief, or the detailed top-up tax computation.
## Ask the client first

- **What kind of person is the business?** A company (LLC, free zone company, branch), a sole establishment or freelancer (natural person), or a partnership? Subject to exemptions, a juridical person is in scope without the natural-person turnover test; a natural person only above AED 1,000,000 of business turnover in a calendar year. ([Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Legislation/05-06-2023/3/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2049%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf))

- **Financial year end and first tax period.** This sets the return and payment deadline (9 months after the period ends). **Revenue for this period and for every earlier tax period.** Small Business Relief fails permanently once any period's revenue has been over AED 3,000,000. ([Ministerial Decision No. 73 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Corporate%20Tax/Ministerial%20Decision%20No.%2073%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf))

- **Is the business part of a multinational group?** Ask for group consolidated revenue. A constituent company of a multinational group, as defined in Cabinet Decision No. 44 of 2020 (groups within Cabinet Decision No. 44 of 2020), cannot use Small Business Relief ([Ministerial Decision No. 73 of 2023, Article 3](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Corporate%20Tax/Ministerial%20Decision%20No.%2073%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf); [Small Business Relief Guide](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Guides/CT/Small%20Business%20Relief%20Guide%20-%20EN%20-%2029%2008%202023.pdf)). Screen groups against the top-up-tax scope below; this is not a determination of liability. ([Cabinet Decision No. 142 of 2024](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Cabinet-Decision-No-142-of-2024-on-Top-up-Tax-on-MNEs.pdf)) **Free zone?** Which free zone, what activities, who the customers are (free zone persons, mainland businesses, individuals), whether audited accounts exist, and whether the company has elected out of the QFZP regime.

- **Corporate Tax registration.** The date registered, the registration deadline, and whether a late registration penalty was imposed. **Returns already filed or due**, especially for periods ending 31 December 2025 (the due date, 30 September 2026, has passed, so check for late penalties).

- **Losses brought forward**, the period they arose in, and any ownership change of more than 50% since then. ([Corporate Tax Law](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf)) **Interest expense and EBITDA**, if net interest is large.

- **Related party and connected person transactions:** owners, directors, family members, group companies, and payments to them. **Entertainment, fines, owner drawings and personal expenses** in the accounts.
## The method, step by step

1. **Decide whether the person is a Taxable Person.** A resident juridical person, including a free zone company, is within Article 11, subject to Article 4 exemptions. A natural person is one only if their business turnover is more than AED 1,000,000 in the calendar year, not counting wages, personal investment income or real estate investment income. Check exemptions (government entities, qualifying public benefit entities, qualifying funds and others under Article 4) and refer them out. ([Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Legislation/05-06-2023/3/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2049%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf))

2. **Check registration.** Every Taxable Person registers on EmaraTax by the deadline in FTA Decision No. 3 of 2024 (table below), including businesses that will claim Small Business Relief and free zone companies.

3. **Fix the tax period.** It is the financial year, meaning the Gregorian calendar year or the 12-month period for which financial statements are prepared (Article 57). Changing it needs an application to the FTA (Article 58).

4. **Test Small Business Relief** for a resident person. Revenue must be AED 3,000,000 or less in this period *and in every previous period*. The period must start on or after 1 June 2023 and end on or before 31 December 2029 (MD 131/2026 Article One). The person must not be a QFZP or a constituent company of a multinational group. If eligible and the client wants it, elect it on the return. Taxable income is then treated as nil and a simplified return is filed. ([Ministerial Decision No. 73 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Corporate%20Tax/Ministerial%20Decision%20No.%2073%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf))

5. **For a free zone company, test QFZP status**: adequate substance, qualifying income, the de minimis test, arm's length compliance with transfer pricing documentation, audited financial statements, and no election out. If any condition fails, it is taxed like a mainland company for that period and the next four.

6. **Compute taxable income** (Article 20): start from accounting net profit under the accounting standards accepted in the UAE; standards/cash-basis eligibility is held below. Remove exempt income (for example qualifying dividends and participation income, Articles 22-23). Add back non-deductible items: 50% of entertainment, fines, bribes, owner drawings, Corporate Tax itself, recoverable input VAT, and donations to bodies that are not qualifying public benefit entities (Articles 28, 32, 33). Apportion mixed personal and business costs. ([Corporate Tax Law](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf))

7. **Apply the general interest limitation** for persons in scope of Article 30, after the separate Article 31 test and historical-debt/infrastructure exclusions; for a 12-month period with net interest expense above AED 12,000,000: the deduction is the higher of AED 12,000,000 and 30% of tax-adjusted EBITDA. The excess carries forward for 10 periods. Pro-rate the monetary threshold for a non-12-month period. ([Ministerial Decision No. 126 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2023/Ministerial%20Decision%20No.%20126%20of%202023%20on%20the%20General%20Interest%20Deduction%20Limitation%20Rule%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf))
8. **Adjust related party and connected person transactions to arm's length** (Articles 34-36).

9. **Deduct brought-forward losses**, oldest first, up to 75% of taxable income before loss relief (Article 37). ([Corporate Tax Law](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf))

10. **Apply the rates**: 0% on the first AED 375,000 of taxable income and 9% on the rest. A QFZP pays 0% on qualifying income and 9% on all other taxable income, with no AED 375,000 band. ([Corporate Tax Law](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf))

11. **Take credits in statutory order:** withholding tax credit first, then foreign tax credit capped at UAE tax on the same income (unused foreign credit is neither carried forward nor back), then applicable other incentives or relief credits, then pay the residual (Articles 44, 46-47).
12. **File and pay within 9 months** of the end of the period on EmaraTax, and keep records for 7 years.
### Rates and thresholds for 2026

### Rates ([Corporate Tax Law, Article 3](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf); [Cabinet Decision No. 116 of 2022](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Corporate%20Tax/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%20116%20of%202022%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf); [Free Zone Persons bulletin](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2024/CT%20Bulletin/Basic%20Tax%20Information%20bulletin-%20Free%20Zone%20Person-English.pdf))
| Who | Taxable income | Rate | Source |

| Taxable Person (not a QFZP) | Portion not exceeding AED 375,000 | 0% | https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Corporate%20Tax/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%20116%20of%202022%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf |

| Taxable Person (not a QFZP) | Portion exceeding AED 375,000 | 9% | https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Corporate%20Tax/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%20116%20of%202022%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf |
| Qualifying Free Zone Person | Qualifying Income | 0% | https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf |

| Qualifying Free Zone Person | All taxable income that is not Qualifying Income (no AED 375,000 band) | 9% | https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf |

| Non-resident with no permanent establishment or nexus | UAE-sourced income, as withholding tax | 0% | https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf |

- The AED 375,000 band is given once per Taxable Person per tax period, however many businesses it runs. Artificial separation that brings the combined zero-rated taxable-income amount above the band is subject to the anti-abuse rule; the FTA considers legitimate commercial purpose and the financial, economic and regulatory ties (Cabinet Decision No. 116 of 2022, Article 2).

- A multinational group in scope of top-up tax pays extra tax under the UAE GloBE computation, using the 15% minimum rate; exclusions, adjustments and safe harbours mean this is not simply 15% of accounting profit (Corporate Tax Law, Article 3(3)). See the top-up tax section.

### Natural persons ([Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Legislation/05-06-2023/3/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2049%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf); [Small business bulletin](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2026/CT_TaxB_ulletin_EN_V5.pdf))
| Rule | Detail |
| Threshold | Total business turnover (gross income) **more than** AED 1,000,000 in a Gregorian calendar year |
| At or below AED 1,000,000 | Not subject to Corporate Tax and not required to register |
| Never business income | Wages; personal investment income; real estate investment income that does not need a licence |
| Relationship to Small Business Relief | The AED 1,000,000 registration threshold is separate from the AED 3,000,000 relief threshold |

### Small Business Relief ([Corporate Tax Law, Article 21](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf); [Ministerial Decision No. 73 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Corporate%20Tax/Ministerial%20Decision%20No.%2073%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf); [Ministerial Decision No. 131 of 2026](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ministerial-Decision-No.-131-of-2026-Amending-Certain-Provisions-of-Ministerial-Decision-No.-73-of-2023-on-Small-Business-Relief-for-the-Purposes-of-Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-EN.pdf))
| Condition or effect | Rule |
| Who | A Resident Person that is a Taxable Person, natural or juridical |
| Revenue test | Revenue of AED 3,000,000 or less in the current tax period **and in every previous tax period**; one period over the threshold ends eligibility for good |

| Periods covered | Tax periods starting on or after 1 June 2023 and ending on or before 31 December 2029 (extended from 31 December 2026 by Ministerial Decision No. 131 of 2026, issued 29 July 2026) |

| Excluded | A Qualifying Free Zone Person; a constituent company of a multinational group under Cabinet Decision No. 44 of 2020 (apply the constituent-company definition in Cabinet Decision No. 44 of 2020; do not substitute the distinct master/local-file threshold) |
| How | Register, then elect in the tax return for **each** period; it is not automatic |
| Effect | Treated as having no taxable income; simplified return; no Corporate Tax |

| What switches off | Exempt income, reliefs, deductions, tax loss relief and transfer pricing documentation (Article 55) do not apply in a relief year. Transactions must still be at arm's length when measuring revenue |
| Losses | A loss of a relief year cannot be carried forward. Losses from earlier non-relief years cannot be used in a relief year but survive for later non-relief years |
| Interest | Net interest expenditure of a relief year cannot be carried forward; earlier disallowed interest survives for non-relief years |
| Anti-splitting | Artificially splitting a business to stay under AED 3,000,000 is treated as tax avoidance |
| Accounts | NON-OPERATIVE HOLD: confirm MD 114/2023 cash-basis eligibility separately before using cash accounts |

Revenue means gross income under the accounting standards applied, not profit ([Small Business Relief Guide](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Guides/CT/Small%20Business%20Relief%20Guide%20-%20EN%20-%2029%2008%202023.pdf)). The FTA's small business bulletin still says periods ending on or before 31 December 2026. Ministerial Decision No. 131 of 2026 replaces that text, so rely on the Decision.

### Qualifying Free Zone Persons ([Cabinet Decision No. 100 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%20100%20of%202023%20on%20Determining%20Qualifying%20Income%20for%20the%20Qualifying%20Free%20Zone%20Person%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf); [Ministerial Decision No. 229 of 2025](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2025/MD-No-229.pdf); [Free Zone Persons bulletin](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2024/CT%20Bulletin/Basic%20Tax%20Information%20bulletin-%20Free%20Zone%20Person-English.pdf))

A Free Zone Person is a juridical person incorporated, established or registered in a free zone. Individuals and unincorporated partnerships cannot be Free Zone Persons. A Free Zone Person is a QFZP only while it meets **all** of these conditions (Corporate Tax Law, Article 18):

- It keeps adequate substance in the free zone or designated zone: core income-generating activities carried on there, with adequate assets, qualified full-time staff and operating costs. Outsourcing follows the free-zone/designated-zone location and supervision conditions. For Qualifying Intellectual Property, Article 8(3) permits outsourcing anywhere in the UAE or to an unrelated person abroad, with adequate supervision.
- It derives Qualifying Income.
- It has not elected to be taxed at the standard rates.
- It complies with the arm's length principle and keeps transfer pricing documentation.
- It prepares audited financial statements.
- Its non-qualifying revenue does not exceed 5% of total revenue or AED 5,000,000, whichever is lower (the de minimis test in Ministerial Decision No. 229 of 2025, Article 3).

**Qualifying Income** is income from transactions with other Free Zone Persons (who must be the beneficial recipients), except income from Excluded Activities. It also includes income from transactions with anyone for Qualifying Activities, qualifying intellectual property income, and other income while the de minimis test is met.

**Excluded Activities** generate non-qualifying revenue for the de minimis test; satisfying de minimis can still bring other income into Qualifying Income under Cabinet Decision No. 100 of 2023, Article 3(1)(d):
- transactions with natural persons, except for ships, fund management, wealth management and aircraft leasing;
- banking;
- insurance, other than reinsurance and captive insurance within headquarter services;
- finance and leasing, subject to the exceptions in MD 229;
- ownership or exploitation of immovable property, other than commercial property in a free zone let to a Free Zone Person.

Always taxed at 9% even for a QFZP: income of a domestic or foreign permanent establishment (for example a mainland branch), most immovable property income, and non-qualifying intellectual property income.

**Consequence of failing:** failure of a condition removes QFZP status from the start of that period and for the next four periods (MD 229/2025 Article 5). An election to use standard rates takes effect from the current or following period under Corporate Tax Law Article 19; the election-duration rules are a separate unconfirmed hold below.

A QFZP distributing goods in or from a designated zone also needs an agreed-upon procedures report from its auditor, for periods starting on or after 1 January 2026 ([FTA Decision No. 6 of 2026](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/2026/FTA%20Decision%20No.%206%20of%202026%20on%20Determining%20the%20Additional%20Procedures%20for%20the%20Compliance%20of%20QFZP%20-%20for%20publishing%20-%2007%202026.pdf)).
### Deductions and add-backs ([Corporate Tax Law, Articles 28, 32 and 33](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf))
| Item | Treatment |
| Expenses wholly and exclusively for the business, not capital | Deductible when incurred |
| Mixed business and personal expenses | Only the business part, identified or apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis |
| Entertainment of customers, shareholders, suppliers (meals, accommodation, transport, admission, facilities) | 50% deductible |
| Fines and penalties (other than compensation for damages or breach of contract) | Not deductible |
| Bribes and illicit payments | Not deductible |
| Dividends and profit distributions to owners | Not deductible |
| Amounts withdrawn by a natural person Taxable Person or a partner | Not deductible |
| Corporate Tax; foreign tax on income; recoverable input VAT | Not deductible |
| Donations to bodies that are not Qualifying Public Benefit Entities | Not deductible |
| Payments to connected persons (owners, directors, their related parties) | Deductible only up to market value and only if wholly and exclusively for the business |

### Losses ([Corporate Tax Law, Articles 37-39](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf); [FTA losses bulletin](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2026/CT-Tax-Bulletin-Corporate-Tax-Losses-EN.pdf))
- Tax losses carry forward with no time limit. The set-off in a later period is capped at 75% of that period's taxable income before loss relief.
- The oldest losses go first. Losses must be used to the fullest extent possible each period; the client cannot choose to use less.
- No relief for losses from before Corporate Tax started, from before the person became taxable, or from exempt activities.
- After an ownership change of more than 50%, losses survive only if the same or a similar business continues. This test does not apply to listed companies.

- Transfer of losses to a group company needs 75% common ownership, both resident juridical persons, neither exempt nor a QFZP, the same year end and the same accounting standards. The ownership must run continuously from the start of the loss period to the end of the utilisation period (Article 38(1)(d)). The 75% cap applies to own and transferred losses together.
- For how losses interact with Small Business Relief, see that section.

### Interest limitation ([Corporate Tax Law, Article 30](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf); [Ministerial Decision No. 126 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2023/Ministerial%20Decision%20No.%20126%20of%202023%20on%20the%20General%20Interest%20Deduction%20Limitation%20Rule%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf))
| Rule | Detail |
| Net interest expenditure | Interest expense (including amounts carried forward) minus taxable interest income |
| Safe amount | No limit where net interest expenditure does not exceed AED 12,000,000 for a 12-month period (pro-rated for longer or shorter periods) |
| Above the safe amount | Deduct the higher of AED 12,000,000 and 30% of EBITDA (excluding exempt income) |
| Disallowed excess | Carried forward for the next 10 tax periods, oldest first |
| Not applied to | Banks, insurance providers, and natural persons carrying on a business |

| Separate rule | Interest on related party loans used for dividends, capital returns, capital contributions or acquisitions of related parties is not deductible, unless the taxpayer can show the main purpose of the loan and the transaction is not to gain a Corporate Tax advantage. No advantage is deemed where the related party lender is itself subject to Corporate Tax, or a similar foreign tax, on the interest at a rate not less than 9% (Article 31(1)-(3)) |

### Transfer pricing and related parties ([Corporate Tax Law, Articles 34-36 and 55](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf); [Ministerial Decision No. 97 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/05-06-2023/2/Ministerial%20Decision%20No.%2097%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf); [Tax Returns Guide](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Guides/CT/CT-Returns-EN-11-11-2024.pdf))

- Transactions with **related parties** must be at arm's length, priced with one of the five OECD methods (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, profit split) or another method where none of those works. This applies to domestic transactions as well as cross-border ones.
- **Related parties** include:
- individuals related to the fourth degree of kinship or affiliation;
- an individual and a company where the individual, alone or with related parties, owns 50% or more or controls it;
- companies with 50% or more common ownership or control;
- a person and its permanent establishment;
- partners in the same unincorporated partnership;
- trustees, founders and beneficiaries of trusts and foundations.

- **Control** includes the ability to exercise 50% or more of voting rights, determine 50% or more of the board, receive 50% or more of profits, or otherwise exercise significant influence over the business and affairs (Article 35(2)(d)).
- **Connected persons** are the owners, directors and officers, and their related parties. Payments to them are deductible only at market value. This does not apply to listed or regulated taxpayers.

- **Disclosure in the return:** complete the related party schedule when the total value of all related party transactions is more than AED 40 million, and disclose each category over AED 4 million. Dividends between related parties are excluded from both thresholds; report gross income and expenditure separately (Tax Returns Guide section 16.1). Complete the connected person schedule where payments or benefits with a connected person together with its related parties exceed AED 500,000; report each qualifying person separately (Tax Returns Guide sections 9.3 and 16.2).

- **Master file and local file:** required where the taxpayer's revenue in the period is AED 200,000,000 or more, or it belongs to a multinational group with consolidated revenue of AED 3,150,000,000 or more. The local-file inclusion/exclusion conditions in MD 97/2023 Article 2(2)-(6) must also be tested; a file threshold does not mean every transaction belongs in it. Documents must be produced within 30 days of an FTA request, or the later date directed by the FTA.

### Domestic minimum top-up tax, summary only ([Cabinet Decision No. 142 of 2024](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Cabinet-Decision-No-142-of-2024-on-Top-up-Tax-on-MNEs.pdf); [FTA Decision No. 12 of 2026](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2026/legislation/FTA%20Decision%20No.%2012%20of%202026%20on%20Registration%20and%20Deregistration%20Timelines%20-%2008%202026.pdf))

- **Who:** UAE constituent entities of a multinational group whose ultimate parent's consolidated financial statements show annual revenue of EUR 750 million or more in at least two of the four fiscal years immediately before the tested year.
- **From when:** fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2025.
- **What:** a top-up tax computed under the annex's UAE GloBE rules using the 15% minimum rate, with adjustments, exclusions and safe harbours; do not calculate it as 15% of accounting profit.
- **Registration:** within 7 months after the end of the first fiscal year in scope. Entities with a fiscal year ending before 30 April 2026 register on or before 30 November 2026.
- **Top-up tax return:** due 15 months after the end of the fiscal year, or 18 months for the fiscal year that is the first transition year (Article 8.1.2).

- **Pillar Two information return:** due 15 months after the end of the fiscal year. The decision gives no longer first-year period for this return (Article 15.4). The FTA may change these requirements, so check before relying on them.
The computation is specialist work, so refer it out (see "When to refuse or refer").
## Boundary and exception table
| Situation | Outcome |
| Individual with business turnover of exactly AED 1,000,000 | Not in scope (the test is "exceeds") |
| Individual with salary plus rental income from personally held property, no licence | Not business income; no Corporate Tax, no registration |
| Company with taxable income of exactly AED 375,000 | Tax nil (0% applies to the portion not exceeding AED 375,000) |
| Revenue exactly AED 3,000,000 | Still eligible for Small Business Relief (the test is "does not exceed") |
| Revenue above AED 3,000,000 in any earlier period | Small Business Relief never available again |
| Business with revenue under AED 3,000,000 that forgets to elect | Taxed normally; the election is made period by period on the return |
| Free zone company, non-qualifying revenue exactly at the lower of 5% or AED 5,000,000 | Passes (the test is "does not exceed") |

| Free zone company selling to individuals | Normally Excluded Activity and non-qualifying revenue for de minimis; MD 229/2025 Article 2(2)(a) excepts the specified ship, fund management, wealth management and aircraft activities |
| Free zone company with a mainland branch | Branch income taxed at 9% with no AED 375,000 band |
| QFZP claiming Small Business Relief | Not allowed |
| Net interest expenditure of exactly AED 12,000,000 | Fully deductible (limit applies only above it) |
| Loss brought into a Small Business Relief year | Not used that year; still available in a later non-relief year |
## Worked cases
The amounts are illustrations. Each case uses a calendar-year tax period unless stated.
1. **Freelance consultant, Small Business Relief.**

- **Facts:** a Dubai mainland sole establishment owner had business revenue of AED 1,400,000 in 2024; in 2025 it was AED 2,600,000 and in 2026 it was AED 2,900,000. Turnover passed AED 1,000,000 in 2024, so she was a Taxable Person and had to register by 31 March 2025.

- **Relief:** revenue has been AED 3,000,000 or less in 2026 and in every earlier period, the 2026 period ends before 31 December 2029, and she is not in a multinational group. So she can elect Small Business Relief on her 2026 return, due 30 September 2027. Taxable income is treated as nil and the tax is nil.

- **If she forgets to elect:** with taxable income of AED 900,000, tax is (AED 900,000 − AED 375,000) × 9% = AED 47,250 ([Cabinet Decision No. 116 of 2022](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Corporate%20Tax/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%20116%20of%202022%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf)).
2. **Relief lost for good; standard computation.**
- **Facts:** an Abu Dhabi engineering LLC had revenue of AED 3,200,000 in 2025 and AED 4,200,000 in 2026. Its 2026 taxable income after all adjustments is AED 2,380,000.

- **Relief:** if revenue fell to AED 2,400,000 in 2027, Small Business Relief would still not be available, because 2025 revenue exceeded the threshold ([Ministerial Decision No. 73 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Corporate%20Tax/Ministerial%20Decision%20No.%2073%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf)).
3. **Loss cap and entertainment.**

- **Add-backs:** a company's 2026 accounting profit is AED 800,000. It includes AED 60,000 of client entertainment and an AED 5,000 traffic fine. Add back 50% of the entertainment (AED 30,000) and the whole fine: AED 800,000 + AED 30,000 + AED 5,000 = AED 835,000.

- **Loss cap:** it has AED 700,000 of losses from 2024 and 2025. The cap is AED 835,000 × 75% = AED 626,250. Taxable income becomes AED 835,000 − AED 626,250 = AED 208,750, which falls inside the AED 375,000 0% band, so the tax is nil. The remaining AED 73,750 of losses carries forward.

- **If it had elected Small Business Relief instead:** had its revenue allowed it to elect the relief in 2026, none of the AED 700,000 could be used in 2026, but all of it would survive for later non-relief years ([FTA losses bulletin](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2026/CT-Tax-Bulletin-Corporate-Tax-Losses-EN.pdf)).
4. **Interest limitation.**
- **Facts:** a property developer has net interest expenditure of AED 20,000,000 and tax-adjusted EBITDA of AED 50,000,000.

- **Limit:** 30% of EBITDA is AED 50,000,000 × 30% = AED 15,000,000, which is higher than AED 12,000,000, so AED 15,000,000 is deductible. The other AED 5,000,000 carries forward for up to 10 periods ([Ministerial Decision No. 126 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2023/Ministerial%20Decision%20No.%20126%20of%202023%20on%20the%20General%20Interest%20Deduction%20Limitation%20Rule%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf)).
5. **QFZP that passes de minimis, with a mainland branch.**
- **Branch:** the branch's AED 500,000 of taxable income is taxed at 9% with no AED 375,000 band: AED 500,000 × 9% = AED 45,000.

- **If the test had failed:** had sales to individuals been AED 1,200,000, it would fail and be taxed at the standard rates for 2026 and the four following periods ([Free Zone Persons bulletin](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2024/CT%20Bulletin/Basic%20Tax%20Information%20bulletin-%20Free%20Zone%20Person-English.pdf)).
6. **Free zone software house selling to the mainland.**
- **Facts:** a free zone software company earns AED 5,000,000, all from mainland companies.

- **Outcome:** assume the receipts are ordinary development-service fees, with no qualifying intellectual-property income. Those services are not a listed Qualifying Activity, so all of that revenue is non-qualifying and far above the de minimis limit. It is not a QFZP. It pays 0% on the first AED 375,000 of taxable income and 9% above that, like a mainland company ([Ministerial Decision No. 229 of 2025](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2025/MD-No-229.pdf)).
7. **Late registration waived.**

- **Facts:** a company incorporated on 10 February 2026 with a 31 December year end had to register within 3 months, by 10 May 2026. It registered in August 2026, so the AED 10,000 late registration penalty applies.

- **Waiver:** if it files its first return (period ending 31 December 2026) within 7 months, by 31 July 2027, the FTA waives the penalty, or refunds it to the EmaraTax account if it was paid. The tax itself is still due within 9 months, by 30 September 2027 ([CTP006](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2025/CTP006-Waiver-of-Late-Registration-Administrative-Penalty-02-07-2025.pdf)).
8. **Freelancer below the threshold, and a salaried landlord.**

- **Freelancer:** a freelance designer with AED 750,000 of business turnover in 2026 is not subject to Corporate Tax and does not register. Monitor turnover, because once it exceeds AED 1,000,000 in a calendar year she must register by 31 March of the next year.

- **Salaried landlord:** an employee who owns two flats and rents them out without a licence has no Corporate Tax at all. Wages and real estate investment income are not business income ([Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Legislation/05-06-2023/3/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2049%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf)).
9. **Late return and late payment.**
- **Facts:** the return for the year ended 31 December 2025 was due 30 September 2026 but was filed, with AED 100,000 of tax paid, on 15 December 2026.
- **Late filing:** AED 500 is charged on 1 October, 1 November and 1 December: 3 × AED 500 = AED 1,500.

- **Late payment:** 14% a year, charged monthly for each month or part, on the unpaid tax. That is about AED 100,000 × 14% ÷ 12 × 3 = AED 3,500. EmaraTax computes the exact amount, so confirm it there ([Cabinet Decision No. 75 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2075%20of%202023%20and%20amendments%20-%20For%20Publishing.pdf)).

## When to refuse or refer
- **Business structure unknown.** Stop until you know whether the client is a juridical person, a natural person, a partnership or a branch. The rules differ at every step.
- **Salaried employee asking about income tax on salary.** There is no Corporate Tax on wages; answer that and stop.

- **QFZP determinations** where the activities, customer mix or substance are unclear, or where the de minimis test is close. Never apply 0% without evidence of every condition and audited accounts. Refer to an FTA-registered tax agent. ([Corporate Tax Law](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf))

- **Top-up tax** for groups with EUR 750 million or more of revenue: the scope, the computation, the safe harbours and the information return. Refer to a Pillar Two specialist. ([Cabinet Decision No. 142 of 2024](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Cabinet-Decision-No-142-of-2024-on-Top-up-Tax-on-MNEs.pdf))
- **Tax groups, loss transfers, qualifying group transfers, business restructuring relief, and participation exemption** claims.
- **Transfer pricing documentation**, advance pricing agreements, or related party transactions near the disclosure thresholds.
- **Non-residents:** permanent establishment or nexus questions, effective management and control, withholding tax and treaty relief.

- **Exempt persons**: government-controlled entities, public benefit entities, investment funds, pension funds, extractive businesses. For the categories and applications within its Articles 2 and 5, exemption procedure follows [FTA Decision No. 15 of 2026](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/2026/FTADecisionNo15Of2026onProvisionsonExemptionFromCorporateTax.pdf), in force from 15 September 2026.
- **Voluntary disclosures, tax assessments, reconsideration requests**, or unfiled past periods.
- **Unincorporated partnerships and family foundations.**
- **Research and development incentives or tax credits**, which fall outside this skill.
## Filing and payment

### Registration deadlines ([FTA Decision No. 3 of 2024](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/RE%20FTA%20Decision%20No.%203%20of%202024%20on%20Registration%20Timeline%20for%20Corporate%20Tax%20%20-%20For%20publishing.pdf); [Small business bulletin](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2026/CT_TaxB_ulletin_EN_V5.pdf))
| Person | Register by |
| UAE juridical person incorporated on or after 1 March 2024, including a free zone company | 3 months from incorporation or establishment |
| Foreign company effectively managed and controlled in the UAE (from 1 March 2024) | 3 months from the end of its financial year |
| Non-resident with a permanent establishment (from 1 March 2024) | 6 months from the date the permanent establishment exists |
| Non-resident with a nexus (from 1 March 2024) | 3 months from the date of the nexus |
| Resident individual whose business turnover exceeds AED 1,000,000 in a calendar year (2024 onwards) | 31 March of the following year |
| Non-resident individual with turnover above the threshold | 3 months from meeting the conditions |
| UAE juridical persons existing before 1 March 2024 | Deadlines by licence month ran from 31 May to 31 December 2024 and have passed |
Businesses claiming Small Business Relief and free zone companies must register too. Registering for VAT does not register the business for Corporate Tax.

### Returns and payment ([Corporate Tax Law, Articles 48, 53, 56](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf); [Ministerial Decision No. 84 of 2025](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2025/MD-No-84-of-2025.pdf))
- File the return and pay the tax within 9 months of the end of each tax period, on EmaraTax. Businesses electing Small Business Relief file a simplified return by the same date.

- Audited financial statements are required for a Taxable Person (not a tax group) with revenue exceeding AED 50,000,000 in the period, and for every QFZP. This applies to periods starting on or after 1 January 2025.
- Keep records for 7 years after the end of the tax period they relate to.
| Tax period ends | Return and payment due |
| 31 March 2026 | 31 December 2026 |
| 30 September 2026 | 30 June 2027 |
| 31 December 2026 | 30 September 2027 |

### Earlier returns: periods ending in 2025 ([Corporate Tax Law, Articles 48 and 53](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf))
| Tax period ended | Return and payment due |
| 31 March 2025 | 31 December 2025 |
| 31 December 2025 | 30 September 2026 |

The same rates, the AED 375,000 band and the Small Business Relief conditions apply to 2025 periods. For a 2025 period, the Small Business Relief threshold also applied under the original 31 December 2026 end date, so the extension changes nothing for 2025. Audited statements are required above AED 50,000,000 of revenue for periods starting on or after 1 January 2025.

### Penalties ([Cabinet Decision No. 75 of 2023 and amendments](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2075%20of%202023%20and%20amendments%20-%20For%20Publishing.pdf); [CTP006](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2025/CTP006-Waiver-of-Late-Registration-Administrative-Penalty-02-07-2025.pdf))
| Violation | Penalty (AED) |
| Late registration | AED 10,000. Waived (or refunded) if the first return is filed within 7 months of the end of the first tax period, instead of 9; applies to the first tax period only |
| Late return | AED 500 a month or part month for the first 12 months, then AED 1,000 a month or part month |
| Late payment | 14% a year, charged monthly for each month or part, on the unpaid tax from the day after the due date |
| Incorrect return corrected before the filing deadline | No penalty; otherwise AED 500 |
| Voluntary disclosure of an error | 1% of the tax difference for each month or part from the original due date |

| Failure to disclose an error before audit notification | 15% of the tax difference, plus 1% per month or part; the end date depends on whether a disclosure is later submitted or an assessment is issued (Decision 75/2023 table item 11) |
| Failure to keep records | AED 10,000, or AED 20,000 for a repeat within 24 months |
| Late deregistration application | AED 1,000 a month, up to AED 10,000 |
| Failure to update the tax record | AED 1,000, or AED 5,000 for a repeat within 24 months |
## Completion checklist ([Corporate Tax Law, consolidated](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf))
- [ ] Business structure and residence confirmed; natural person turnover test (more than AED 1,000,000) applied, excluding wages and investment income.
- [ ] Registration date checked against the deadline; late registration waiver considered.
- [ ] Tax period and filing deadline (end + 9 months) recorded.

- [ ] Small Business Relief tested on current **and all previous** periods' revenue (AED 3,000,000), period end on or before 31 December 2029, no MNE or QFZP status; election made on the return if wanted.
- [ ] Free zone: every QFZP condition evidenced, de minimis test computed (lower of 5% or AED 5,000,000), branch and property income taxed at 9%.
- [ ] Entertainment limited to 50%; fines, owner drawings, personal costs and Corporate Tax added back.
- [ ] Interest limitation applied above AED 12,000,000.
- [ ] Related party and connected person transactions at arm's length; disclosure schedules and master/local file thresholds checked.
- [ ] Losses applied oldest first, capped at 75%; ownership changes checked.
- [ ] Rates applied: 0% up to AED 375,000, 9% above; QFZP non-qualifying income at 9% with no band.
- [ ] Audited statements obtained where revenue exceeds AED 50,000,000 or the person is a QFZP.
- [ ] Top-up tax scope checked for multinational groups (EUR 750 million) and referred out.
- [ ] Return filed and tax paid on EmaraTax; records kept for 7 years.

# UAE payroll for tax year 2026: wages outside Corporate Tax, what the employer's tax return and VAT return do with payroll, and the pension, gratuity and insurance points to confirm
## Scope and who this is for

This skill is for anyone running or advising on a UAE payroll in calendar year 2026: an employer, a payroll provider, or an accountant answering "what do I deduct from this salary, and what does the company owe?". The operative federal tax rules were read in the precise scopes listed in Sources on 1 November 2026; social execution remains held.
What it covers:
- Why wages are outside Corporate Tax, and where the line sits between an employee (no tax) and a self-employed person (possible Corporate Tax).
- How the employer's own Corporate Tax return treats salaries, benefits, directors' pay and pension contributions.
- How the employer's VAT return treats goods and services given to staff, including the rule that changes on 1 October 2026.
- NON-OPERATIVE HOLD: pension coverage, gratuity, the Wage Protection System and unemployment insurance. This Guide does not establish any employee's coverage or run those calculations.

**Social compliance is held, including coverage.** GPSSA/Abu Dhabi pension routing, nationality and first-insurance rules, gratuity coverage and accrual, free-zone differences, WPS, unemployment insurance, rates, caps, due dates and penalties have not been confirmed from their governing sources in this repair. Do not use the old text to execute payroll. Obtain current authority confirmation through a UAE payroll specialist before processing those items. Original details remain in the immutable evidence and destination table.

Companion Skills: Corporate Tax for the employer is in `ae-corporate-tax`; the individual's own position (including when a self-employed person must register) is in `ae-income-tax`; VAT registration and returns are in `uae-vat`.

### What UAE payroll does and does not involve ([Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023, Articles 1 and 2](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Legislation/05-06-2023/3/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2049%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf); [CTGTNP1, section 3.8.1](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Guides/CT/Taxation%20of%20natural%20persons%20-%2025%2011%202023.pdf); [CTGDTI1: Determination of Taxable Income](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Pdf/2024/Determination%20of%20Taxable%20Income%20-%2031%2007%202024.pdf))

**Wage exclusion from Corporate Tax.** Cabinet Decision 49/2023 excludes a natural person's Wage from Corporate Tax; a natural person's Wage is outside it "regardless of the amount of Turnover". There is no Corporate Tax calculation or Corporate Tax return on those wages. This does not determine a worker's foreign-country obligations or social deductions.

**What counts as a wage.** The official definition is wide: "the wage that is given to the employee in consideration of their services under the employment contract, whether in cash or in kind, payable annually, monthly, weekly, daily, hourly, or by piece-meal, and includes all allowances, and bonuses in addition to any other benefits provided for, in the employment contract or in accordance with the applicable legislation in the State". Allowances, bonuses, benefits in kind and benefits due under UAE legislation (such as the statutory end-of-service gratuity) all fall inside it.

**No withholding tax either.** Corporate Tax Law Article 45 sets a 0% withholding rate for a non-resident's State Sourced Income not attributable to its UAE permanent establishment or nexus, subject to the Cabinet's power to specify another rate or category. Wage remains excluded under Decision 49/2023. This Guide does not decide a cross-border recipient's PE, nexus or treaty position.

**Employee or not is a question of fact.** The FTA says "whether a natural person is an employee and earns a salary or other form of remuneration as such, is a question of fact to be determined on a case-by-case basis". A person working under an employment contract is paid a Wage. A person who works for themselves and is not employed by the payer is running a Business, and if that person's business turnover exceeds AED 1,000,000 in a calendar year, that person is within natural-person Corporate Tax scope; apply registration and relief rules before calculating tax. The payer withholds nothing either way; the obligation is the contractor's own.

**Directors' fees.** "Generally, director fees will not be considered as a Business or Business Activity, and therefore would not be subject to Corporate Tax." Where a director is also an employee, the FTA's example treats both the salary and the board fees as a Wage.
**What payroll does involve:**
| Obligation | Who it applies to | Who runs it | Status in this skill |
| Income tax withholding | Nobody | None | Not applicable; wages outside Corporate Tax |
| Corporate Tax deduction for payroll | Employers that are Taxable Persons | FTA | Covered below |
| VAT on staff benefits | VAT-registered employers | FTA | Covered below |
## Ask the client first
- Is the worker employed under an employment contract, or engaged as a contractor or freelancer? If a contractor, how much business turnover do they have in the calendar year?

- What is the worker's nationality: UAE national, another GCC nationality, or expatriate? Keep this for the specialist's coverage check. For a UAE national: in which emirate are they employed? Pension-fund routing is held pending authority confirmation. For a UAE national: when were they first insured? The coverage and regime are held pending authority confirmation.
- Is the employer on the mainland or in a free zone, and which authority licensed it? Ask the specialist to establish the applicable employment and payroll regime.
- Is the employer a Taxable Person for Corporate Tax, and what is its Tax Period? Is it VAT-registered?

- Which benefits does the employer give beyond cash salary: accommodation, health insurance (and for which family members), cars, flights, staff events? Does the employer pay into a private pension or end-of-service savings fund for staff? How much, and has it actually been paid in the Tax Period?
- Are any employees or directors also shareholders, or related to shareholders?
## The method, step by step

1. Classify each person. Employment contract means Wage; no tax is withheld. Self-employed means the person handles their own Corporate Tax position, and you withhold nothing. If you cannot tell, treat it as a question of fact and look at the contract and how the work is done, not the label on the invoice ([CTGTNP1, section 3.8.1](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Guides/CT/Taxation%20of%20natural%20persons%20-%2025%2011%202023.pdf)).
2. Before running payroll, resolve the social-compliance holds with a UAE payroll specialist. This Guide supplies no pension deductions, gratuity accrual, WPS timetable or insurance instruction.

3. For the employer's Corporate Tax return, deduct payroll costs as Business expenditure, test related-party pay at Market Value, and cap private pension fund contributions at the limit shown under the figures below ([CTGDTI1](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Pdf/2024/Determination%20of%20Taxable%20Income%20-%2031%2007%202024.pdf); [Ministerial Decision No. 115 of 2023](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Ministerial-Decision-No.115-of-2023-on-Private-Pension-Funds-and-Private-Social-Security-Funds-for-Corporate-Tax-Purposes.pdf)).

4. For the employer's VAT return, block input tax on goods and services given free to staff for their personal benefit unless an exception applies, and apply the stricter accommodation wording to supplies from 1 October 2026 ([VAT Executive Regulation, Article 53](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/2026/Law-No-8-of-2017-and-its-amendments--09-2026.pdf); [Cabinet Decision No. 149 of 2026, as consolidated](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/2026/Law-No-8-of-2017-and-its-amendments--09-2026.pdf)).
5. File and pay each item on its own timetable (see "Filing and payment" below) and keep the payroll records that support the Corporate Tax deduction.

### VAT on what the employer gives to staff ([VAT Executive Regulation, Article 53, as amended](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/2026/Law-No-8-of-2017-and-its-amendments--09-2026.pdf); [Cabinet Decision No. 149 of 2026, as consolidated](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/2026/Law-No-8-of-2017-and-its-amendments--09-2026.pdf))
The payroll question for VAT is the input tax a VAT-registered employer pays on things it buys and hands to staff.

**The general block.** Input tax is non-recoverable "Where Goods or Services were purchased to be used by employees for no charge to them and for their personal benefit including the provision of entertainment services", unless one of the listed exceptions applies.

**Earlier periods:** the pre-1 October 2026 labour-law and contract/policy exception wording is a non-operative hold: its earlier standalone source did not open. Obtain the historical text before correcting an earlier return.

**What changes from 1 October 2026.** The September 2026 consolidated Executive Regulation records amendments to exceptions (1) and (2) by Cabinet Decision No. 149 of 2026. The Decision is "effective from 1 October 2026". The new texts:

- (1) now reads "Where the provision of those Goods or Services to the employees is mandatory under the applicable labour legislation in the State or any free zone, including financial and non- financial free zones, provided that this does not include the accommodation provided by the employer to its employees, unless the provision of such accommodation is mandatory pursuant to the decisions or directives issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation."

- (2) now reads "Where it is a contractual obligation or documented policy to provide those Goods or Services to the employees, in accordance with the cases and conditions specified by the Authority."

Article 53(1)(c)(3) also permits health insurance, including enhanced cover, for the employee, one spouse and up to three children younger than 18, without prejudice to the labour-law exception. Article 53(1)(c)(4) covers a provision that is a deemed supply. These exceptions remain subject to the normal invoice, payment, business-use and other VAT recovery conditions.
What this means in practice:

- **Staff accommodation.** From 1 October 2026 the labour-law exception no longer covers accommodation unless a MOHRE decision or directive makes it mandatory. Under exception (2), recovery needs a contractual obligation or documented policy and all the conditions of case 3 or case 4 in the list below. The block only matters where the accommodation carries VAT, such as a hotel stay or a hotel or serviced apartment, which are not "residential buildings" (Executive Regulation, Article 37(2)). Unless zero-rated, a lease of a residential building is exempt "where the lease is more than 6 six months or the tenant of the property is a holder of an ID card issued by Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship" (Article 43(1)), so an ordinary long staff flat lease has no input tax to block.

- **Contract or policy benefits generally.** The old test (needed for the role, and normal business practice) is replaced by the six cases in [FTA Decision No. 17 of 2026](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2026/legislation/FTA%20Decision%20No.%2017%20of%202026%20on%20the%20Cases%20and%20Conditions%20for%20the%20Recovery%20of%20Input%20Tax%20Incurred%20on%20Employee%20Expenses%20-%20Publishing.pdf), issued 9 September 2026 and in force from 1 October 2026 (the FTA publishes it as an unofficial translation). A benefit outside these cases is not within exception (2):
1. **Transport:** only between home and work or client premises, or directly for the job; not for personal benefit; the employee cannot opt for cash instead.

2. **Food and drink:** the home is remote, distant or isolated; no suitable food preparation facilities at home or work and no nearby restaurants; linked to the work or required residence period; no cash option.

3. **Accommodation:** no cash option; tied to operational needs and not part of benefits or ordinary pay; the work requires living near the workplace, site or client; for the employee alone, with no family or personal use, unless the employee must live permanently near the workplace so that this is the usual home; commensurate with the job and basic needs, with no significant recreational or personal elements.
4. **New employees' accommodation:** temporary, no longer than 30 days, and commensurate with the job and basic needs.

- **Health insurance.** Recovery continues for the employee, one spouse and up to three children under 18. Input tax on cover for a fourth child, or a child aged 18 or over, falls outside exception (3) and is blocked unless another exception applies.
- **Entertainment of non-staff.** Input tax on entertainment for customers, potential customers, officials, shareholders or investors stays blocked for non-government employers.

Timing: the new texts and FTA Decision No. 17 of 2026 apply from 1 October 2026; where a cost straddles that date, check with the FTA which text governs it. The changes to the input-tax apportionment rules in the same Decision start later, from the first tax year commencing after 1 October 2027; they are not payroll rules and are covered in `uae-vat`.

### Corporate Tax on payroll costs for the employer ([CTGDTI1, sections 4.5.2 and 4.5.10](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Pdf/2024/Determination%20of%20Taxable%20Income%20-%2031%2007%202024.pdf); [Ministerial Decision No. 115 of 2023, Article 5](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Ministerial-Decision-No.115-of-2023-on-Private-Pension-Funds-and-Private-Social-Security-Funds-for-Corporate-Tax-Purposes.pdf); [CTGEPF1: Pension Funds and Social Security Funds](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Guides/CT/Exempt%20Persons%20-%20Public%20Benefit%20Entities%20Pension%20Funds%20and%20Social%20Security%20Funds%20-%2001%2012%202023.pdf))

- **Pay and benefits are deductible.** "Employee costs are generally considered to be wholly and exclusively incurred for Business purposes provided that they are not excessive". It does not matter whether an employee is paid in cash or in benefits such as a car, medical insurance or a flight allowance for family.

- **Related-party pay is tested at Market Value.** Subject to the Article 36(6) listed/regulated-person exceptions, salary or bonus paid to directors, officers or owners "would be deductible ... but only insofar as this salary corresponds with the Market Value rates for such services rendered". Any excess is added back.

- **Staff events are not entertainment.** Staff parties, away-days and performance rewards are employee costs and fully deductible. A private event, such as a family wedding for relatives who happen to work there, is not.

- **Private pension fund contributions.** An employer "may deduct the total value of contributions made to a private pension fund in respect of its employees who are Pension Plan Members in the Tax Period in which such contributions are paid", capped at 15% of that member's total deductible remuneration for the Tax Period. Contributions not paid in the period, or above the cap, are added back.

- **Funds that hold the gratuity.** A private social security fund is "a fund created by a private employer for the purposes of providing statutory end of service gratuity payments to employees". Such a fund, and a private pension fund, can apply to the FTA to be an Exempt Person if it meets the conditions. Public pension and social security funds can also apply for exemption.
## Boundary and exception table
| Situation | Treatment | Watch for |
| Employee under an employment contract, any nationality | Wage; no tax withheld | Social coverage, fund routing and deductions are held for specialist confirmation |
| Allowances, bonuses, benefits in kind | Part of the Wage; no tax | VAT input tax on the benefit may be blocked |
| Director who is also an employee | Salary and board fees both typically a Wage | Related/connected-person pay is tested under Articles 34-36, including Article 36(6) exceptions |
| Non-executive director paid fees | Generally not a Business Activity; no Corporate Tax | Confirm the facts; a director running a separate advisory business is different |
| Freelancer or contractor, business turnover not above AED 1,000,000 in the calendar year | No Corporate Tax registration for that person | The payer still withholds nothing |

| Freelancer or contractor, business turnover exceeds AED 1,000,000 in the calendar year | Taxable Person; registers and files Corporate Tax | The test is "exceeds", so exactly AED 1,000,000 is not over it; Wage, Personal Investment income and Real Estate Investment income do not count towards it |
| Health insurance for employee, one spouse, up to three children under 18 | VAT input tax recoverable (exception 3) | A fourth child or a child aged 18 or over is outside the exception |

| Staff accommodation supplied from 1 October 2026 | VAT input tax blocked unless mandatory under MOHRE decisions, or within case 3 or case 4 of FTA Decision No. 17 of 2026 | A cash option defeats case 3. Matters only for accommodation that carries VAT (hotel, hotel or serviced apartment); a residential lease over six months or to an Emirates ID holder is exempt, so there is no input tax |
| Private pension fund contribution | Deductible when paid, up to the 15% cap per member | Unpaid or excess contributions are added back |
## Worked cases

**Case 1: expatriate employee on the mainland.** A Dubai mainland company employs an expatriate on a monthly salary with housing and transport allowances. Corporate Tax result: no Corporate Tax deduction from wages; lawful social and other payroll deductions require a separate determination, because the whole package is a Wage. Social deductions, gratuity, WPS and insurance remain on hold until current coverage and execution instructions are obtained from the relevant authority or specialist. The salary and allowances are deductible in the company's Corporate Tax return if not excessive.

**Case 2: UAE national employee.** The same Wage exclusion applies. This Guide does not determine the pension fund, coverage, rates, deductions or payment timetable. Resolve the social holds before running the payroll.

**Case 3: private pension fund contributions over the cap.** In its 2026 Tax Period a company pays AED 120,000 into a private pension fund for one employee who is a Pension Plan Member. The employee's total deductible remuneration for the period is AED 600,000. The cap is 15% of AED 600,000 = AED 90,000. The company deducts AED 90,000 and adds back AED 30,000 (AED 120,000 less AED 90,000). Had any of the AED 120,000 been accrued but not paid in the period, that part would also be added back for this period.

**Case 4: consultant paid by invoice.** A company engages a self-employed consultant who invoices AED 1,200,000 in calendar year 2026 and has no employment contract. The payments are not a Wage. The company withholds nothing. The consultant's business turnover exceeds AED 1,000,000, so the consultant is within natural-person Corporate Tax scope; registration, relief and the final tax calculation must be tested separately (route the consultant to the `ae-income-tax` skill). The company deducts the fees as a business expense, at Market Value if the consultant is a related party.

**Case 5: health insurance and accommodation, VAT-registered employer.** An employer buys family health cover for an employee with a spouse and four children (ages 4, 9, 14 and 19) and, from October 2026, pays for a serviced apartment for the employee. Input tax on the cover for the employee, spouse and the three children under 18 is recoverable under exception (3). The cover for the 19-year-old is outside exception (3), so its input tax is blocked unless another exception applies. A serviced apartment is excluded from the residential-building definition. In this example assume its supplier makes a standard-rated taxable supply; the exclusion itself does not establish registration or every other VAT condition. Input tax on the October 2026 serviced-apartment charge is blocked unless a MOHRE decision or directive makes that accommodation mandatory, or a contract or documented policy provides it and every condition of case 3 of FTA Decision No. 17 of 2026 is met (or case 4, for a new employee, up to 30 days). If the employee could take a housing allowance instead, or the apartment is part of the ordinary package, it fails case 3. Had the employer instead leased an ordinary residential flat for more than six months (or to a tenant holding an Emirates ID card), the lease would be exempt: there would be no input tax on the rent, and the Article 53 change would not arise.

**Case 3 variant: part unpaid.** Same facts, but AED 40,000 of the AED 120,000 was accrued and not paid in the period. AED 80,000 was paid, which is under the AED 90,000 cap, so the company deducts AED 80,000 and adds back AED 40,000.

**Case 6: executive director with board fees.** An employee who is a senior manager also sits on the board and receives board-meeting fees. Following the FTA's own example, both the salary and the fees are typically a Wage, so neither is taxed. If the director is also a shareholder, the company deducts the pay only to the extent it matches Market Value.

## When to refuse or refer

- Refer any employee who also has UAE business income, or a contractor near the AED 1,000,000 turnover line, to the `ae-income-tax` skill ([Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023, Article 2](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Legislation/05-06-2023/3/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2049%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf)).
- Refuse to present the employer's pension, gratuity or insurance figures as confirmed by this skill. It does not contain them.
- Refer tax obligations of the employee in their home country (for example, citizens of countries that tax worldwide income) to that country's rules; UAE payroll does not handle them.

## Filing and payment ([Corporate Tax Law, Articles 48 and 53](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Federal-Decree-Law-No.-47-of-2022-and-its-amendments-en-v13.1.26.pdf); [Cabinet Decision No. 149 of 2026, as consolidated](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/2026/Law-No-8-of-2017-and-its-amendments--09-2026.pdf))
- **Employee Corporate Tax:** wages alone produce no Corporate Tax return or payment.
- **Pension contributions:** NON-OPERATIVE HOLD for coverage, fund routing, deduction, frequency, due date and late-payment consequences.

- **Employer's Corporate Tax:** payroll costs go into the employer's Corporate Tax return, which is filed, and any tax paid, no later than nine months after the end of the Tax Period. For a calendar-year company, the 2026 return is due by 30 September 2027. Details are in `ae-corporate-tax`.

- **Employer's VAT:** input tax on staff benefits is claimed only when the VAT recovery conditions are met, in the first eligible period or the next period under VAT Law Article 55. Apply the amended Article 53 texts to periods from 1 October 2026. Details are in `uae-vat`.

### Earlier returns: calendar year 2025 ([Ministerial Decision No. 115 of 2023](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Ministerial-Decision-No.115-of-2023-on-Private-Pension-Funds-and-Private-Social-Security-Funds-for-Corporate-Tax-Purposes.pdf); [Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Legislation/05-06-2023/3/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2049%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf))

The 2025 Corporate Tax return of a calendar-year company was due by 30 September 2026. The payroll rules above were the same in 2025: Wage outside Corporate Tax, employee costs deductible if not excessive, private pension contributions deductible when paid up to the 15% cap. The VAT change of 1 October 2026 does not affect 2025 VAT periods; historical exception wording is held for separate confirmation before correcting those periods.

## Completion checklist ([Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Legislation/05-06-2023/3/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2049%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf); [Ministerial Decision No. 115 of 2023](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Ministerial-Decision-No.115-of-2023-on-Private-Pension-Funds-and-Private-Social-Security-Funds-for-Corporate-Tax-Purposes.pdf))
- [ ] Every worker classified as employee or self-employed, with the contract on file.
- [ ] No tax deducted from any Wage.
- [ ] Social coverage and fund routing independently confirmed from current authority sources; no social instruction is taken from held old text.
- [ ] Gratuity coverage, accrual and payment method independently confirmed before execution.
- [ ] Related-party salaries checked against Market Value.
- [ ] Private pension contributions: paid in the period and within 15% of each member's deductible remuneration; any excess added back.

- [ ] VAT input tax on staff benefits reviewed against Article 53, using the texts in force from 1 October 2026 for later costs; claims on transport, food, accommodation, phones and parking tested against FTA Decision No. 17 of 2026; exempt residential leases carry no input tax to claim.
- [ ] Health insurance recovery limited to the employee, one spouse and up to three children under 18.
- [ ] Contractors near the AED 1,000,000 turnover line told to check their own Corporate Tax position.
